request.recipient: Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting as sole Article II.7.5 administrator at withdrawal, with a later possible transition target to a dOSPO legal entity subject to governance.
request.what: Establish a one-year independent Cardano dOSPO and Open Maintenance Framework program to manage open source sustainability funds, operate advisory councils, form a 501(c)(3) public charity, fund maintenance retainers, and publish public reporting.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 4,094,000 ADA over 12 months to run four programs: Maintenance Fund, Maintainer Development, CodeForUs bounties, and Ecosystem Activation Reserve.
Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting is designated as the sole administrator at the moment of treasury withdrawal, with final allocation authority during the program term.
Mill Law Firm is designated as the independent financial auditor on a quarterly cadence through month 12.
The proposal says no disbursements will be made unilaterally because advisory council feedback will be published before each allocation, while final authority remains with the administrator.
The proposal states that governance can replace the administrator or shut down the initiative through an on-chain Info Action and that remaining funds can be returned if governance is unsatisfied.
The Maintenance Fund would deploy 2,000,000 ADA over 12 months to fund Cardano open source infrastructure selected by dependency centrality, bus factor, and a published priority formula.

The proposer claims Cardano critical tooling, libraries, governance tools, developer infrastructure, and ecosystem services rely on fragmented coordination, volunteer effort, short-term grants, or individual organizations.

The proposer claims a track record building Cardano open source governance at Intersect, including OSPO design, contribution frameworks, maintainer support, and policy leading to the Paid Open Source Model.

The proposal cites external studies and examples, including Harvard D3 Institute, Linux Foundation, Tidelift, CNCF LFX Mentorship, and POSM, to support the need for open source sustainment and contributor programs.

The proposal sets KPIs including 15 or more high-centrality projects funded, 40% top-50 dependency coverage by month 12, 5% trusted committer conversion within 18 months, maintainer attrition below 15% annually, security assessment under 48 hours, and four quarterly reports.

summary: The anchor describes a large one-year treasury-funded open source sustainability program with named administrator, auditor, governance oversight mechanisms, advisory councils, dependency-based funding methods, reporting obligations, and several quantitative KPIs, but many assertions about need, track record, partner alignment, and institutional readiness are stated rather than evidenced inside the document.
